_about: Page changes switched on for a share of films at a time (scripts/lib/rollout.js). Stages: 10, 25, 50, 100 — 'percent' is the share now; a 'schedule' moves it up on the dates given. Set percent and schedule to 0 to turn a change off.

honest-not-announced.what: 'hasn't been announced' -> 'No OTT release date in our sources yet'; titles 'Awaiting Date' (lib/honest.js) — switched to 100% at once on 27 Oct at the owner's request

intent-titles.what: overseas cinema run: 'Release Date in <country>: <date> · Streaming <window>'; out a year+: no 'OTT Release Date' in the title (lib/filmpage.js filmTitleTag) — switched to 100% at once on 27 Oct at the owner's request

one-score.what: one rating, count and FilmyChill Score per film across editions: the freshest TMDB count any edition holds (lib/migrate.js shareScore) — switched to 100% at once on 27 Oct at the owner's request

lean-page.what: every fact once: rating only in the score ring, count once, platform in the answer box first, runtime/genre/language in the header, one skip list, Story after the cast (lib/filmpage.js LEAN_PAGE) — switched to 100% at once on 27 Oct at the owner's request

google-hide.what: catalogue pages Google never showed (google-hidden.json, 90 days to 23 Oct): googlebot noindex, out of the sitemaps and hreflang; Bing and visitors keep them (lib/googlehide.js). Dry run 25 Oct confirmed all 11,887 eligible; switched to 100% at once on 25 Oct at the user's request.

visible-similar.what: "If you liked this" links pages Google can see first (lib/graph.js relatedFilms visible option); older pages redone once per share step (lib/relrefresh.js REL_VERSION 3) — switched to 100% at once on 27 Oct at the owner's request

redesign-v2.what: the film-page redesign v2 (lib/pagev2.js): header and hero on --deep with a breadcrumb, score pill, call to action in four states, Share and Remind me, provenance strip, episode progress bar, click-to-load trailer, sticky Watch bar, dark mode. Presentation only; preview first, then 100% in one switch. Switched to 100% at once on 28 Oct 2026 at the owner's request after the preview.

wiki-reception.what: the score card's Critics row cites its figures: Rotten Tomatoes / Metacritic with counts and the published ratings' count and median, dated to the Wikipedia read (lib/reception.js, lib/editorial.js parseAggregates). Dry run first. Switched to 100% at once on 28 Oct 2026 at the owner's request after the mock-up.

tidy-names.what: one name per service in a film page's where-to-watch pills, FAQ and links ('Prime Video', not 'Amazon Prime Video' + 'Amazon Prime Video with Ads'), on pages Google sees (~236; lib/filmpage.js, rules.js dedupeProviders). Fingerprint v3 reads names the same way, so no date moves — once the stored fingerprints are upgraded to v3, which the builds before 30 Oct 12:00 UTC do; it switches itself on at the 30 Oct 13:52 UTC build.

page-v3.what: film page v3 (owner's sequence, 28 Oct 2026): backdrop, title with status tag, meta line, audience + platform pills, score card with one Audience/Critics line, full Story, director, cast, Good to know (with the where-to-watch row), episodes, trailer, franchise, similar, FAQ. No answer card, CTA, prose fillers, fit rows or separate Where to watch block. Mock-up first. Switched to 100% at once on 28 Oct 2026 at the owner's request after the mock-up.
